data.narrative:
Xanadu Quantum Technologies is a public-stage quantum computing company that has raised $245M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of four same-sector, same-stage quantum computing companies: IonQ ($13.0B), D-Wave Quantum ($6.3B), Rigetti Computing ($4.5B), and Infleqtion ($1.9B).

The peer-median method was applied given the availability of comparable public quantum computing companies. The median valuation across the four peers is $5.4B, with a range spanning $1.9B at the low end (Infleqtion) to $13.0B at the high end (IonQ). This method serves as the primary triangulation anchor, reflecting current market pricing for publicly traded quantum hardware and software platforms at comparable development and commercialization stages.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $4.6B to $6.2B, centered on a median of $5.4B. This narrow band reflects limited methodological diversity—only peer-median comparables are available—and notable dispersion within the peer set itself. Key uncertainties include the relevance of the $13.0B IonQ valuation as an outlier, the timing and maturity differences across peers, and the absence of revenue or profitability-based metrics to ground multiples. Further diligence on near-term commercialization milestones and capital efficiency relative to peers would refine the range.
